{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABVxAyIQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzg_TO8s", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 65, "title": "Add independent OPUS-MT and TranslateGemma 4B translation nodes with Playground tests", "body": "## Problem

The Node Playground currently has only the ReazonSpeech speech-to-text processor. To validate the composable text-processing architecture, we want two independent browser-local Japanese/English translation processors for practical quality/latency comparison: a lightweight OPUS-MT implementation and a quality-oriented TranslateGemma 4B implementation.

Different model implementations must be **separate nodes**, not options in one model-switching node. Each should have its own simple Node Playground page that runs the actual processor.

## Expected outcome

Add two real, independently usable translation processor nodes:

- **OPUS-MT Translation Node** — small, local translation model, preferably via Transformers.js / ONNX Runtime Web.
- **TranslateGemma 4B Translation Node** — local browser WebGPU execution using an available compatible model/runtime, with explicit unsupported-device handling.

Each node accepts text and produces translated text through the existing typed Node/Port pipeline, and each has a dedicated Playground page linked from the index.

Start with Japanese → English; include English → Japanese only when a compatible verified model/runtime exists for that node. If a chosen checkpoint is one-directional, expose a separate direction-specific node or clearly scope it to that direction. Do not pretend a single checkpoint supports both directions.

## Scope

- Investigate and pin concrete compatible model IDs/revisions, tokenizer/runtime versions, required assets, supported language directions, model sizes and license/distribution terms **before** wiring either model. Document choices and limitations.
- Implement a simple text-input/text-output port contract, without generic provenance metadata. Node-specific settings may include target language only where actually supported; no model selector.
- Run heavyweight local inference in a dedicated Worker owned by each processing node. Reuse the existing async start/receive/stop/drain/dispose lifecycle and cancellation semantics; do not introduce a shared model manager.
- Use WebAssembly/WebGPU as supported by each concrete implementation. Keep model execution local; do not send input text to a translation server.
- Expose output through the real Node/Port pipeline. Handle zero/one/multiple asynchronous outputs and cancellation without stale output; preserve order or explicitly document/test the ordering policy.
- Add two separate Playground entries and test pages with a text input, Run, translated output, loading/status/error indication and basic latency measurement. Pages should exercise the actual nodes, not duplicate translation code.
- Avoid forcing the Speech-to-Text Playground layout or controls onto text translation pages.
- Add deterministic unit/browser tests of node ports, worker messages, lifecycle, errors, repeat/cancel and Playground navigation; where feasible add opt-in real-model browser smoke tests with fixed Japanese/English fixtures and clearly distinguish them from translation-quality evaluation.
- Keep the existing Speech-to-Text Playground, Chrome extension and ASR pipeline working.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- Both nodes are separately implemented and separately listed in Node Playground, with no shared model selector.
- The chosen OPUS-MT and TranslateGemma checkpoints, versions, licenses, asset sizes, directions and supported browser capabilities are documented and pinned.
- Each node accepts text through a declared input port and emits translated text through a declared output port; a deterministic pipeline test exercises each node and its real worker adapter.
- Each test page invokes its production node and displays the translation, status/errors and basic latency.
- Real model initialization and at least one supported Japanese → English translation run are verified for each node in a suitable browser environment. Do not substitute only mocked inference for this acceptance check; clearly report device/WebGPU constraints and any skipped checks.
- No user text is sent to a remote inference endpoint; any model downloads are explicit and documented.
- Unsupported WebGPU, model-load failure, offline/cache failure, cancellation and repeated runs are handled without stale results or leaked resources.
- The shared Pipeline runtime remains free of model-specific logic; no extra generic framework, editor or model manager is added.
- Relevant unit/browser/extension tests pass, with heavy real-model checks separately documented.

## Required post-merge verification

After the merged revision is deployed to GitHub Pages, verify the index and both new test pages are reachable, with correct asset URLs under the repository prefix. Record the deployed SHA and run URL. If real-model verification on the deployed origin is needed because of browser model-fetch restrictions, record it as pending until performed; do not claim completion prematurely.

## Context

- #7 — local-first composable pipeline vision.
- #57 — Node/Port runtime.
- #63 — Node Playground index and Speech-to-Text node page.
- OPUS-MT: https://huggingface.co/Helsinki-NLP
- TranslateGemma: https://huggingface.co/google/translategemma-4b-it
- Browser proof-of-concept reference: https://github.com/webml-community/TranslateGemma-WebGPU

This Issue adds two concrete processors and their independent test pages. Translation quality comparison is a subsequent user evaluation, not a subjective merge gate.
